hypothesis: Projecting exact conflict files into the native CLI sandbox and retaining runtime-owned pending merges will recover Codex builder work without weakening the shared merge gate.

metricsCompared.name: pending-merge continuation eligibility
metricsCompared.baseline: successful owner run excluded and claim continuation rejected
metricsCompared.candidate: retained lineage accepted by dispatcher and claim continuation

metricsCompared.name: ambiguous in-scope native resolution
metricsCompared.baseline: accepted after a non-error edit session and mechanical path checks
metricsCompared.candidate: needs-review after deny-all resolved-diff and task-scope judgment, with claim and merge retained

metricsCompared.name: validation ordering
metricsCompared.baseline: resolver output staged and merge committed before canonical reconciliation validation
metricsCompared.candidate: changed-path and marker checks, validation on the unmerged working tree, then runtime staging and commit

metricsCompared.name: destructive conflict dispatch
metricsCompared.baseline: delete/modify and branch-side rename conflicts could be classified as textual
metricsCompared.candidate: unmerged index stages and both-side rename ancestry keep destructive conflicts in needs-review

metricsCompared.name: focused regression suite
metricsCompared.baseline: 269 builder and Git tests in the superseded fallback decision
metricsCompared.candidate: 133 affected tests across 20 files plus a trusted-host focused run of 85 tests across 15 changed behavioral suites; the synthetic lifecycle and shipped Codex OS-boundary case both pass

rationale: A production-shaped native-contract fixture starts from a continued pending-merge claim whose prior terminal finalizer recorded recoveryRequested:false, resolves and reviews the conflict, validates before resolver staging or merge commit, reconciles canonical, merges through the normal gate, releases the claim, removes the worktree, and leaves no recovery projection. Adversarial fixtures keep failed validation, ambiguous intent, out-of-scope edits, delete/modify states, and branch-side renames fail-closed. The shipped Codex fixture no longer accepts a chmod fallback and passed on the trusted host with live denial across both physical Git metadata roots. Promotion remains held only until the committed mechanism is reloaded to complete the live 44f5972e merge, claim transition, and cleanup.
